items.claim: B2 headline: the time inside a provider-minted request id, with one constant skew per stream, must fall between the stream's last input and the response's first output
items.closest_work: Vanini et al. forensic time anchors (arXiv 2412.12814); Willassen 2008 clock-hypothesis test; Roughtime draft-17 s8.2; Jaeger ClockSkew adjuster
items.what_it_does: Each covers two of the three ingredients. Id or external time checked against the local clock: time anchors, Magnet AXIOM. Causal bracket with a skew allowance: Willassen Thm 2, Jaeger, NTP. Chained external times with a radius, where a violation means malfeasance: Roughtime, but its times are signed.
items.what_it_does_not: No opened source combines all of it on a recorded, uninstrumented log: an unsigned id-embedded server clock, one existential constant offset per stream, and infeasibility used as a per-record tamper flag.
items.deciding_citation: arXiv 2412.12814 time-anchor definition (a mismatch between internal and external timestamps 'indicates tampering'); Willassen 2008 Theorem 2; absence across the 35 sources B2b opened. Risk: Vanini 2024b full text was not opened.

items.claim: B2 application: LLM-provider request ids as the external clock for agent tool-log stamps, plus the single-response binding test
items.closest_work: Langfuse ai-gateway and Codex rollout-trace, which store the provider id next to their own clock; debug-claude-session skill; ccusage
items.what_it_does: Systems record provider ids and use them for correlation, support lookup, dedupe and grouping. ccusage deduplicates resume/fork copies by (message.id, requestId).
items.what_it_does_not: None of the 25 systems examined decodes the id as a clock or uses any provider-side clock to verify, order or bound tool-log stamps.
items.deciding_citation: B2c, 0 of 25 systems (langfuse mapping.rs L183-189 stores the id as metadata only; codex rollout-trace reducer/inference.rs L211-217 stores it only). debug-claude-session SKILL.md: 'Correlate by time + model, not request id.'

items.claim: B2 fact: provider request/response id layouts are documented and stable
items.closest_work: Anthropic errors doc and SDK types/message.py; OpenAI API reference overview; Vertex prediction_service.proto and Gemini generative_service.proto
items.what_it_does: Documents that the ids exist. Anthropic and OpenAI explicitly reserve the right to change id format and length. Vertex says response_id 'is the encoding of the event_id'.
items.what_it_does_not: No vendor documents any layout or timestamp. Every clock is inferred: Anthropic req_/msg_ as UUIDv7; OpenAI chatcmpl base62 epoch and resp_ time-first hex; Gemini as the Google ei layout with a validated microsecond field; Meta resp_ hex seconds. At least 3 unannounced format changes were observed. This is a MATERIAL LIMITATION.
items.deciding_citation: anthropic-sdk-python types/message.py: 'The format and length of IDs may change over time.' developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview lists 'Changing the length or format of opaque strings, like resource identifiers' as backwards-compatible.

items.claim: B1(a): a residual of duration against expected workload as a fabrication signal in agent tool logs (N1)
items.closest_work: BOINC CreditNew; Sinharay 2020 and van der Linden response-time residuals; DeepLog and Fu 2009; Kovah 2012 timing attestation; CacheWise and Continuum; crewAI PR #3388
items.what_it_does: BOINC treats a reported elapsed time the declared FLOP bound cannot explain as falsification. Psychometrics flags aberrant response times against a workload-conditioned model. Log-AD flags duration residuals. Agent serving systems predict tool duration, but for scheduling. crewAI's unmerged PR flags tool calls under 10 ms as LIKELY_FAKE.
items.what_it_does_not: No source runs a passive, two-sided, workload-conditioned residual with a within-session same-command baseline on recorded agent tool calls, where the threat is fabricated result content.
items.deciding_citation: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/BOINC/boinc/CreditNew.md: incentive to cheat 'by falsifying benchmark scores or elapsed time'; Sinharay 2020 PMC7433384; crewAI tool_execution_verifier.py @7be92705 L164-166

items.claim: B1(b): corr(residual, output_size) as the discriminator between work-bound and generation-bound latency
items.closest_work: Early Bird (arXiv 2409.20002) s4-D; Time Will Tell (arXiv 2412.15431); DistServe
items.what_it_does: Early Bird separates cached from computed responses by whether TTFT is flat or scales with request length (input side, threshold). Time Will Tell measures Pearson(time, output tokens): at least 0.987 locally and 0.370 for GPT-4o via the API.
items.what_it_does_not: No opened source correlates a workload-conditioned residual with output size, or uses size scaling to decide whether a recorded tool result was executed or generated. Three angles called it NOVEL but conditionally; B1c found the inference pattern.
items.deciding_citation: arXiv 2409.20002 s4-D: cache-hit 'TTFT remains consistent, regardless of the request length'

items.claim: B3.1 Token conservation: context growth vs logged appended content as a tamper or fabrication witness
items.closest_work: Velasco et al. arXiv 2510.05181; Paritok arXiv 2609.22114; Hoque et al. arXiv 2605.30040
items.what_it_does: Billing audits compare reported token counts with a recount of the visible text. Paritok shows the per-turn input delta equals the appended slice.
items.what_it_does_not: They trust the content and audit the provider, the reverse of our direction. They do not use recorded agent transcripts and report no tamper curve.
items.deciding_citation: arXiv 2510.05181 s3.2 (reported length minus recount); arXiv 2609.22114 Table 2

items.claim: B3.2 Cache-read chain as a witness that each logged prefix was sent
items.closest_work: KeyPooling arXiv 2608.17485; CacheTracer arXiv 2608.20732; CacheProbe arXiv 2605.30613
items.what_it_does: Uses the provider-reported cached-token count as an oracle that a prefix was sent earlier.
items.what_it_does_not: These are live active probes within the cache lifetime. None reads recorded usage after the fact or chains the counter across one session.
items.deciding_citation: arXiv 2608.17485 s II-A; arXiv 2608.20732 Assumption 1 (Cache Telemetry integrity)

items.claim: B3.3 Prompt-cache timing side channel (Gu et al.) as a witness of what was sent
items.closest_work: Gu, Li, Kuditipudi, Liang & Hashimoto, ICML 2025, arXiv 2502.07776
items.what_it_does: A live TTFT audit with a KS test detects caching and its sharing level.
items.what_it_does_not: Uses no usage fields and no recorded logs, and needs a live cache plus paid probes. It does not overlap B3.1/B3.2 and cannot run on our corpora.
items.deciding_citation: arXiv 2502.07776 s2.1: 'Cache hits tend to have a faster TTFT than cache misses'

items.claim: B3.4 N2 accounting identity: an inline-fabricated result is billed as output tokens

I wrote C:\Swarms\.claude\worktrees\analysis\analysis\PRIOR_ART.md (about 615 lines). It opens with the verdict table, then B2 (§1), then B1 with separate verdicts for sub-claims (a) and (b) (§2), then the B3 items (§3.1–3.11), the B4/B5 internal-embodiment findings (§3.12), what was not covered (§3.13), and conflicts and caveats (§4). Synthesis reasoning is marked [INTERPRETATION]. Every citation is one a Track B agent opened. Unopened sources are marked UNVERIFIED inline and listed in §1.5 and §2.5.

Calls the evidence did not make directly:

- **B1(b) is PARTIAL, not NOVEL.** Three angles reported NOVEL, but each said so only on condition that the other angles found nothing. B1c found the same inference in Early Bird (arXiv 2409.20002 §4-D): telling two producing processes apart by whether latency is flat or scales with length.
- **B2 is split into two verdicts.** The method is PARTIAL: time anchors, Willassen 2008, event-time bounding and Roughtime are all old. The application is NOVEL: no system among the 25 B2c examined uses a provider id or a provider-side clock to check anything.
- **The provider-id layout is undocumented for every provider, and this is a material limitation.** Its section in §1.2 has a per-provider table (documented? timestamp? stable?) and confirming counts from the corpus tasks: TB2 WozCode, hookele, HF Hub, and Meta resp_ ids in OSWorld.

Flags for the orchestrator:

1. **Biggest prior-art risk:** the full text of Vanini et al. 2024b ("Was the clock correct?") was never opened. If its Google-search example bounds the ei time between causally ordered events with a tolerance, the B2 method becomes TAKEN for forensics. Someone with library access should check it.
2. **The brief's N5 premise is false.** "Nobody studies fabricated failures" is contradicted by CEF arXiv 2606.14831, arXiv 2609.14758, arXiv 2607.19449 and Transluce's o3 report. It must be removed from the writeup.
3. **Silent Failure conflicts with CLAUDE_context §7.** Two agents read v1 as reporting XGBoost, which §7 says it does not have. PRIOR_ART.md cites only its transfer AUROCs and does not take a side; a human should reconcile.
4. **Possible held-out exposure.** B2a's aiv_cu scans touched 517 rows / 270 sessions of held-out split H. Only id-format aggregates were computed and no threshold was tuned. Whether this breaks the "nothing reads H" rule is your call.
5. **No Track B verdict for:** FINDINGS rank 2 (image-token ledger), rank 3 (git execution window), and the N5 items for sort order, truncation boundary, whitespace, output-size distribution and cold start. Their novelty stays UNVERIFIED.
6. **Corrections to FINDINGS, suggested only (I did not edit it):**
   - rank 1 novelty line;
   - rank 5 Gu et al. relevance;
   - Gemini id clock resolution is microseconds, not 1 s;
   - the Gladyshev & Patel link is now confirmed through Willassen 2008, though the primary is still unopened.

I made no commits and touched nothing swarm-related. I wrote no files besides PRIOR_ART.md. PRIOR_ART.md points to analysis/CORPUS_INVENTORY.md, which another writer has not produced yet.

items.claim: B2 conjunction: an id-embedded external time bounds a log event between causally ordered local events, with a skew allowance, on a recorded log
items.closest_work: Willassen 2008 §2 and Thm 2–3, which summarises Gladyshev & Patel 2005 and Schatz et al. 2006; Albea 2026 KQL InternetMessageId-date check; Roughtime §8.2; Jaeger clockskew.go
items.what_it_does: Willassen §2 sets bracketing of an uncertain event by externally timed events beside server-clock correlation, and Thm 2–3 test clock hypotheses that include a deviation term. The KQL query flags emails whose id-embedded date and recorded processing time fall on different days, run over recorded logs.
items.what_it_does_not: No source uses a clock embedded in a provider-minted id together with a two-sided causal bracket and a per-stream offset. The KQL check is one-sided, works to the day, and trusts the log over the id. Willassen and Gladyshev work by hand on file-system artifacts.
items.deciding_citation: Willassen08.pdf §2: 'time boundaries can be established when an event that occurred at an unknown or uncertain time is causally preceded and succeeded by events whose times of occurrence are known ... must come from external sources' (https://dl.ifip.org/db/conf/ifip11-9/df2008/Willassen08.pdf). Now labelled near-TAKEN as a method.

items.closest_work: debug-claude-session skill; OTel GenAI gen_ai.response.id; Langfuse gateway; Codex rollout-trace; ccusage; Hearsay App. I; Luo et al. 2605.02187; Qin et al. 2609.30266

items.what_it_does_not: None of them decodes a provider id as a clock, or uses it to bound, order or verify tool-log stamps.

items.closest_work: BOINC CreditNew; Sinharay 2020; Kelly 2005; Kovah 2012; crewAI PR #3388
items.what_it_does: BOINC rejects claims that exceed fpops_bound and names falsified elapsed time as the cheat. Kelly flags response time that disagrees with a workload model. crewAI #3388 labels tool calls under 10 ms LIKELY_FAKE.
items.what_it_does_not: None is a passive, two-sided, workload-conditioned residual on recorded agent tool calls with a within-session baseline. crewAI #3388 is a fixed floor applied live and was never merged.

items.claim: B1(b): corr(residual, output_size) separates work-bound from generation-bound latency
items.closest_work: Early Bird arXiv 2409.20002; Time Will Tell arXiv 2412.15431

items.what_it_does_not: Neither correlates a workload-conditioned residual with output size, and neither applies the idea to tool results.
items.deciding_citation: arXiv 2409.20002 §IV-D: 'when the cache is hit, the TTFT remains consistent, regardless of the request length, whereas when the cache is missed, TTFT increases almost linearly'
